This is what a per-payment custody address would look like, and the vendor documents none of it: no page of docs.allium.so read on 2026-09-11, 09-20, 09-28 or 09-29 mentions Stripe
decoded.feePayer: the Solana entry's extra.feePayer is BENrLoUbndxoNMUS5JXApGMtNykLjFXXixMtpDwDR9SP in all three responses, and was a different value on each earlier date (BFK9TLC3edb13K6v4YyH3DwPb5DSUpkWvb7XnqCL9b4F on 2026-09-11, Hc3sdEAsCGQcpgfivywog9uwtk8gUBUZgsxdME1EJy88 on 09-20, GVJJ7rdGiXr5xaYbRwRbjfaJL7fmwRygFi1H6aGqDveb on 09-28), so it is stable within a reading and not across dates
decoded.feePayer-is-not-the-vendor's: api.bitrefill.com, an unrelated vendor, presented the same address in its own Solana extra.feePayer field in three responses read in the same minute (probe record p-20260929-bitrefill-x402-recipient-stability, filed separately as pull request #196 and not in this diff; Part B of this artifact holds the same lines). That is an observation about what two vendors' documents contain, and it is the whole of what was measured: who controls the address, and whether either vendor does, was not established and cannot be from an HTTP response. A value shared by two unrelated vendors' challenges is consistent with settlement infrastructure they have in common; no page read by this reporter names any such party
decoded.mpp: the Machine Payments Protocol challenge in the same response still names method tempo, intent charge, amount 30000, a currency address on chain id 4217, a five-minute expiry and extra.stripe_mode custody. Its recipient rotates like the other two custody targets: read twice more at 06:15:29Z and 06:15:34Z, five seconds apart, the decoded request document named 0x2ccb30dde62ebfc89c26fc4979512df95068806f and then 0x02235d99992a3cae7b187541fe92119327b082e6, and the 2026-09-11 artifact of the same endpoint names 0x51962043d87ac092d258483762ce5086ebe507f4 (Part C of the artifact)
decoded.free-endpoint: GET https://agents.allium.so/api/v1/supported-chains/realtime-apis/simple answers 200 with no payment, as on every earlier date
decoded.not-measured: no payment was made, no paid retry was attempted, and no earlier address was tested. Whether a payTo read on an earlier date still settles a payment today is therefore unknown: what is measured is that the document no longer quotes it. That the rotation is per payment rather than per request is a reading of the Stripe custody fields and is not established either

finding: Read unpaid three times within ninety seconds on 2026-09-29, the priced endpoint answered 402 with the shape it has had for eighteen days: an MPP challenge and an x402 version 2 document in one response, exact scheme, USDC at 30000 units on Base, Solana, X Layer and Polygon. Inside that unchanged shape, two of the four recipient addresses are not stable. Base and Solana carried a different payTo in each of the three responses, two of them four seconds apart, while X Layer and Polygon carried the addresses of 2026-09-11; the two that rotate are exactly the two carrying Stripe custody fields, as does the MPP recipient, read twice more five seconds apart. So a recipient quoted from any dated record of this surface, including this registry's own, is not the recipient the server quotes now. Whether an older address still settles a payment was not tested and cannot be read off an unpaid request: no payment was made and no paid retry attempted, and that the rotation is per payment rather than per request is a reading of the Stripe fields, not a measurement. One IP is one sample.

reproducibility.command: for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s -D - -o /tmp/b 'https://agents.allium.so/api/v1/developer/tokens/search?q=usdc' | grep -iE '^(HTTP|www-authenticate|payment-required)'; python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('/tmp/b')); [print(a['network'], a['payTo'], (a.get('extra') or {}).get('feePayer')) for a in d['accepts']]"; sleep 2; done  # the status line and the two challenge headers are kept alongside the recipients; the MPP request parameter is base64 and decodes to the document in Part C of the artifact
